title: Sales enablement: positioning, competitive briefs, pitch decks, pricing guidance, case studies, and security FAQ
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview

Purpose: This document provides consolidated sales enablement material for Redwood Inference focused on developer-first positioning and messaging, concise competitive briefs, a recommended pitch deck outline, practical pricing guidance for discovery conversations, short customer case studies for credibility, and a security FAQ for prospect evaluation. Use this as the canonical reference for pre-sales and customer-facing enablement.

Audience: Account executives, solutions engineers, sales engineers, product marketing, and customer success.

Owner: Go-to-market (content owner: Aisha Patel).

Last updated: 2026-12-22

---

1) Positioning & Core Messaging

Short elevator pitch
- Redwood Inference is a developer-first inference platform that delivers predictable, cost-efficient LLM serving across hosted, dedicated, and private deployments—so engineering teams can ship LLM features with production-grade latency, reliability, and cost controls.

Three value pillars (1-line each)
- Production-first performance: Low-latency, high-throughput runtime tuned for real application workloads.
- Economical at scale: Cost-aware controls (batching, caching, quant profiles) and predictable Dedicated capacity.
- Flexible deployment: Same API and operational tooling across hosted, reserved, and private VPC/on-prem environments.

Key proof points to surface in conversations
- Verified benchmarks: <model-specific latency/cost numbers> available in public model catalog and internal benchmark suite.
- Customers: Platform teams, AI-native startups, and regulated enterprises running production chat, summarization, and retrieval-augmented generation.
- Reliability features: rollouts, model fallbacks, and SLA-backed Dedicated options.

Persona-focused messages
- Engineering/ML engineers: Focus on runtime telemetry, SDKs, model version pinning, and custom quantization profiles.
- Platform/Infra teams: Emphasize Dedicated capacity, autoscaling policies, cost forecasting, and IAM/KMS integrations.
- Product leaders/PMs: Highlight predictable unit economics and A/B rollout primitives for controlled quality migrations.

---

2) Competitive brief (TL;DR + how to position against common competitors)

Competitors in scope: managed LLM APIs, cloud-managed endpoints, and self-hosted inference runtimes.

Comparison matrix (high-level)
| Dimension | Redwood Inference | Major cloud-managed endpoints | Self-hosted runtimes |
|---|---:|---|---|
| Time to production | Fast (hosted API + quickstarts) | Fast | Slow (ops burden) |
| Predictable unit cost | High (cost controls, optimize tooling) | Variable (instance-based) | Low at scale but high ops cost |
| Deployment flexibility | Hosted, Dedicated, Private | Hosted (multi-region) | Private/on-prem only |
| Observability & tooling | Token-level cost/latency + rollouts | Basic metrics | Varies widely |
| Security & compliance | Built-in enterprise controls + private deploy | Cloud provider controls | Customer-controlled but heavy lift |

How to position vs managed LLM API providers (e.g., competitor-A)
- If prospect's priority is simple prototyping and minimal infra: acknowledge the competitor's simplicity, then differentiate by calling out Redwood's production features (SLOs, rollouts, billing granularity) that matter once ML features scale.

How to position vs cloud-managed endpoints (e.g., competitor-B)
- Emphasize unified developer experience across hosted and private footprints; showcase cost controls (batching/caching) and the ability to pin model versions and fail over automatically to cheaper variants.

How to position vs self-hosted runtimes (open-source or third-party)
- Lead with reduced operational overhead and faster time-to-value: we provide turnkey Dedicated and Private packages plus curated quantization/compilation profiles that reduce TCO without sacrificing control.

Common objections and rebuttals
- "We can just self-host to save costs." -> Rebuttal: Self-hosting can save compute cost at scale but often requires >6–12 months of engineering effort to reach comparable reliability and observability; Redwood reduces both time and ongoing ops headcount.
- "Your hosted pricing is expensive for high volume." -> Rebuttal: Walk through batching, caching, and Dedicated commit options; show example math (see pricing guidance).

---

3) Recommended pitch deck outline (5–12 slides recommended for discovery)

Suggested slide sequence (with speaker notes summary)
1. Title + logo + one-line mission fit (Why now?)
2. Customer problem (latency, variable costs, operational risk) with short customer quote or metric
3. Redwood value proposition (three pillars) + 2–3 proof points
4. How it works (runtime + smart routing + caching) — keep architecture diagram simple (client -> routing -> runtime pools (hosted/dedicated/private) -> model catalog)
5. Use cases and personas (chat, RAG, personalization, search re-rank)
6. Demo / sample API + code snippet (1–2 slides)
7. Pricing & deployment options (hosted, Dedicated commit levels, Private licensing)
8. Security & compliance highlights (SOC2, KMS, audit logging, VPC)
9. Roadmap & support (SLA tiers, onboarding, implementation timeline)
10. Customer case studies / ROI math (short callouts)
11. Next steps & ask (POC proposal, eval plan, timelines)

Deck tips
- Use concrete numbers in discovery: latency percentiles, cost per 1M tokens, commit discounts.
- Keep technical slides accessible for non-engineers; push deeper runtime/benchmarks to appendix.

---

4) Pricing guidance and discovery math (for AE/SE use)

Pricing constructs to discuss
- Hosted: usage-based (tokens / embeddings) with volume-break discounts and optional burst capacity.
- Dedicated: monthly/annual reserved GPU capacity with throughput SLAs and overage pricing.
- Private: license + support / deployment services (one-time and ongoing maintenance fees).

Discovery checklist (questions to ask to surface correct billing model)
1. Expected request volume (requests/day) and average prompt + response token length.
2. Percent of streaming vs non-streaming requests.
3. Peak QPS and acceptable p99 latency (ms).
4. Data residency or network constraints (VPC/on-prem).
5. Security/compliance requirements (SOC2, HIPAA, ISO).
6. Desired contract term (monthly vs annual commit).

Quick example math (hosted vs dedicated)
- Prospect: 10k requests/day, avg 500 input+output tokens, 30 days = 150M tokens/month.
- Hosted list price: $0.0008 / token = $120,000/month.
- With batching/caching optimizations (25% effective token reduction) = 112.5M tokens -> $90,000/month.
- Dedicated example: 2 x A100-equivalent dedicated pools with monthly commit price $45,000/pool = $90,000/month — plus predictability and SLA.
- Guidance: If expected sustained monthly token usage > 100M, propose Dedicated commit and run a cost comparison as a formal TCO exercise.

Discounting & negotiation playbook
- Reference discount bands by ARR/commit level (example: 10% for 6–12mo pilots, 20–35% for multi-year contractual commitments with minimum 12–24 month commit).
- Offer onboarding credits for pilots with success metrics (e.g., 90-day POC up to $X in credits).

---

5) Short case studies (2x concise one-paragraph summaries)

Case Study: NovaRetail (retail personalization)
- Problem: NovaRetail needed low-latency personalization at checkout across 1200 stores and a web fleet; self-hosting introduced reliability gaps and high ops overhead.
- Solution: Redwood Dedicated with autoscaling policies, prefix caching for common queries, and model quantization profile reduced per-token cost.
- Outcome: p95 latency reduced from 420ms to 85ms; per-interaction inference cost reduced by 46%; deployment time to production cut from 5 months to 6 weeks.

Case Study: Tradeworks (financial search & summarization)
- Problem: Regulated workflows required a private deployment and strict audit logging while maintaining developer velocity.
- Solution: Redwood Private with VPC-only control plane, KMS integration, and audit stream to the customer SIEM.
- Outcome: Completed SOC2 readiness checklist for the product team; achieved compliance sign-off and launched a regulated pilot within 8 weeks.

---

6) Security FAQ for prospects (concise, customer-facing answers)

Q: What certifications and audits does Redwood have?
A: Redwood maintains SOC 2 Type II and ISO 27001 readiness artifacts for our control plane and offers documentation to enterprise customers during security reviews. Private deployments can be deployed behind customer managed controls.

Q: Where is customer data stored and how long is it retained?
A: For hosted customers, data residency is selectable by region (US, EU, APAC regions where available). By default, request logs are retained for 30 days; retention policies can be configured per-customer for Dedicated/Private.

Q: How do you protect encryption keys?
A: We integrate with customer-managed KMS/HSM providers (AWS KMS, Azure Key Vault, GCP KMS) for encryption-at-rest keys; in Private deployments keys remain under customer control.

Q: Can we run Redwood entirely in our VPC / on-prem?
A: Yes. Redwood Private supports VPC-hosted control planes and an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. We provide an engineering runbook for installation, upgrades, and rollback.

Q: How is access controlled?
A: RBAC with SSO integrations (SAML/OIDC), API keys with scoped permissions, and optional token-level auditing. Dedicated customers receive per-route permissioning and fine-grained policy controls.

Q: Do you log prompts/responses?
A: By default, we log metadata for observability and billing (request sizes, latency) and optionally store request/response payloads for debugging. For regulated customers we support zero retention and targeted redaction.

Q: How do we validate model behaviour and prevent regressions?
A: Redwood Optimize includes evaluation hooks and regression alerts tied to prompt sets. Customers can upload their test prompts and receive automated quality monitoring and rollback triggers.

---

7) Playbook: recommended next steps for AE/SE after discovery

1. Rapid cost estimate: complete token math and produce hosted vs Dedicated TCO within 48 hours.
2. Security checklist: surface any required certifications, KMS needs, and region constraints.
3. Pilot scope: propose a 6–12 week pilot with measurable success metrics (latency p95, cost per request, error rate) and define data retention/PII handling.
4. Technical kickoff: schedule SE-led runbook review and provide sandbox keys & quickstart repo.
